chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The teeth and the molars are equal; [the diyah for each is] one-tenth.

key_terms.نِصْفُ الْعُشْرِ: One-tenth (referring to the fraction of full diyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money value for a single tooth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfarayini’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the principle of equality in *diyah* (blood money) for dental injuries, asserting that the compensation for incisors (*san*) and molars (*adras*) is identical. It establishes a fixed rate of one-tenth of the full *diyah* per tooth, reflecting the Shia juristic view that prioritizes uniformity in bodily compensation regardless of the tooth's functional role. This ruling is foundational in *fiqh al-diyah* for calculating injuries to the mouth.
